rows.short_title: El Barrio
rows.additional_description_1:
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 22, 2026 at the 224 West 124th Street Library, Manhattan, at 11:00 am, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed amendments to a deed and land disposition agreement identified below.

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

 

              Address                      Block/Lots            Community District

              53 East 110 Street             1616/123             11

              304 East 126 Street           1802/47               11

              201 East 120 Street           1785/1                 11

              204 West 121 Street          1926/35               10

 

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.                                                                                                      

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 10 for public review at the office of Manhattan Community Board 10 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing.

The hearing location is accessible to individuals using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 788-0010. TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

rows.additional_description_1:
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN THAT A REAL PROPERTY ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSITIONS PUBLIC HEARING, in accordance with Section 824 of the New York City Charter, will be held on October 28, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. via Conference Call No. 1-646-992-2010, Access Code 717 876 299.

 

IN THE MATTER OF a renewal of the lease for the City of New York, as tenant, on the entire fourth and fifth floors of the building located at  105 East 106th Street (Block 1634 & Lot 3), and on the partial fourth floor of the building located at 104 East 107th Street (Block 1634 & Lot 65) in the Borough of Manhattan for the Emergency Hazardous Services and Emergency Repair Services divisions  of the Department of Housing Preservation and Development to use as an office, or for such other use as the Commissioner of the Department of Citywide Administrative Services may determine.

 

The proposed use was approved by the City Planning Commission pursuant to NYC Charter Section 195c on February 19, 1992 (CPC Appl. No. N 920296 PXM, Public Hearing Cal. No. 7).

 

The proposed renewal of the lease shall commence on full lease execution and shall expire on the earlier of (i) twenty (20) years after the Substantial Completion Date, or (ii) twenty-one (21) years after the Commencement Date, at an annual rent of $1,086,960.00 from Lease Execution through Substantial Completion Date, $1,168,482.00 from Substantial Completion Date through the first five (5) years, $1,304,352.00 for the following five (5) years, $1,440,222.00 for the following five (5) years, and $1,576,092.00 for the last five (5) years, payable in equal monthly installments at the end of each month.

 

The lease may be terminated by the Tenant in its entirety at the end of twelfth (12) year from the Commencement Date, provided the Tenant gives the Landlord twelve (12) months prior written notice.  In the event that the lease is terminated by the Tenant, the Tenant shall pay to the Landlord the unamortized portion of both Landlords cost of the alterations, improvements and such portion of the commission paid to Tenant Representative Broker.

 

The Landlord shall prepare final architectural plans and engineering plans and make alterations and improvements in accordance with preliminary architectural plans and specifications which are attached to the lease.  The alterations and improvements consist of Base Building Work, which the Landlord shall provide at its sole cost and expense.

 

Further information, including public inspection of the proposed lease, may be obtained, at One Centre Street, Room 2000 North, New York, NY. 10007. To schedule an inspection, please email RESPublicHearingInquiries@dcas.nyc.gov

 

If you need further accommodations, please let us know at least five business days in advance of the Public Hearing via email at DisabilityAffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at 212-298-0734.

The public hearing will be held via conference call. Call in #1-646-992-2010; Access code: 2342 243 5265

 

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') has proposed the sale of the following City-owned property (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of The Bronx:

 

Address                                                                          Block/Lot(s)

 

501 West 174th Street                                                       2131/50

511 West 171st Street                                                       2128/55

522 West 174th Street                                                       2130/39

         

Under HPD's Affordable Neighborhood Cooperative Program, occupied City-owned residential buildings are purchased by Restoring Communities Housing Development Fund Corporation (Sponsor) and then rehabilitated by a private developer selected through a request for qualifications.  Upon conveyance to the Sponsor, buildings will be managed by the private developers.  Following completion of rehabilitation, Sponsor conveys the building to a cooperative housing development fund corporation (Cooperative Corporation) formed by the buildings tenants.  The cooperative interests attributable to occupied apartments will be sold to the existing tenants for $2,500 per apartment.  The cooperative interests attributable to vacant apartments will be sold for a price affordable to families earning no more than 165% of the area median income.

 

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Sponsor for the nominal price of one dollar per building.  When completed, the project will provide 50 affordable cooperative dwelling units.

 

At the time of sale, the Sponsor will be required to sign a rental regulatory agreement with HPD containing, among other things, restrictions on rents, incomes, and assets.  When the Sponsor conveys the building to the Cooperative Corporation upon the completion of rehabilitation, the Cooperative Corporation will be required to sign a cooperative regulatory agreement with HPD containing, among other things, restrictions on sale prices, incomes, and assets as well as requirements for a flip tax and building reserve fund.

 

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

 

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

rows.short_title: New York City Indirect Source Rule 'WISER' Program
rows.additional_description_1:
New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) proposes to implement a Warehouse Indirect Source Emissions Reduction (WISER) local law that would require large warehouse operators to reduce mobile sources of pollution and/or mitigate the impact of the air pollution associated with their operations in New York City. In accordance with the State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) (Section 8-0113, Article 8 of the Environmental Conservation Law) as set forth in 6 NYCRR Part 617, and the City Environmental Quality Review (CEQR) process, as set forth in Executive Order 91 of 1977 and its amendments, DEP is hereby issuing Notice of Positive Declaration, Intent to Prepare a Draft Environmental Impact Statement, Lead Agency Declaration and Draft Scope of Work.

DEP will hold a virtual public scoping meeting to receive public comments on the Draft Scope of Work on November 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. The Draft Scope of Work, which provides a summary description of the Program and the methodologies to be used in preparing the Draft EIS impact analyses, is available on the DEP website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/about/environmental-reviews.page. You may register for the virtual public meeting at: https://bit.ly/4egU5lY. Comments on the Draft Scope of Work may be presented at the meeting or submitted in writing or by email to:

Dana Taplin, Project Manager

NYC Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Environmental Planning and Analysis

59-17 Junction Boulevard, 4th Floor

Flushing, NY 11373

dtaplin@dep.nyc.gov

Written comments on the Draft Scope of Work will be accepted until December 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM. DEP will subsequently issue a Final Scope of Work, which will include responses to written comments and comments received during the public meeting and may incorporate revisions in response to comments received.

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on November 18, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. The Public Hearing will be held at The Harlem Library, 224 East 125th Street, Manhattan at which time and place those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed deed and land disposition agreement amendments described below

 

Pursuant to Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) has proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (City), located in the Borough of Manhattan and known as:   

 

Address                                          Block/Lot(s) 

 

1678 Park Avenue                          1745/134

                                                       (FKA p/o Lot 32, Lot 33-39, p/o Lot 41)                                                            

1678 Park Avenue was conveyed by the City to NYC Partnership Housing Development Fund Company, Inc. on December 13, 2001, pursuant to a deed and land disposition agreement (LDA). The deed and LDA require compliance with the original Milbank Frawley Circle-East Urban Renewal Plan (Original Plan), approved by the City Planning Commission on August 19, 1992 (C920139HUM) and the New York City Council on October 8, 1992 (Reso. No. 920), which prohibits residential development within 100 feet of Park Avenue and restricts the sites to parking. On November 30, 2017, the Original Plan was amended (Second Amendment) by the New York City Council (Reso. No. 1743) to permit residential use within 100 feet of Park Avenue.

 

The sponsor now intends to develop a proposed project consisting of one 100% affordable residential building financed by NYCHA that will include 222 total units and 80 parking spaces (the Project).

 

To facilitate the Project, HPD intends to modify the deed and LDA. The site is located in the Milbank Frawley Circle East Urban Renewal Area and is identified as a portion of Site 37A within the Plan. The deed and LDA associated with the parcel require compliance with the Original Plan, which specifically prohibits development within 100 feet of Park Avenue. HPD intends to amend the deed and LDA  to remove the restrictions limiting the use of the parcel to parking and require compliance with the Second Amendment, which will be in effect until December 14, 2057, and replace these restrictions with new restrictions that would require that 1678 Park Avenue be developed as a 100% affordable project.

 

A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents will be made available to Manhattan Community Board 11 for public review at the office of Community Board 11 no later than twenty (20) days prior to the public hearing. 

 

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734. TDD users should call Verizon relay services. Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

Pursuant to Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) has proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (City), located in the Borough of Manhattan and known as:  

 

Address                                          Block/Lot(s)

 

1700 Park Avenue                                                            1746 / Lot 33

(FKA p/o Lot 32, Lot 33-39, p/o Lot 41)  

                                                                                            

1700 Park Avenue was conveyed by the City to NYC Partnership Housing Development Fund Company, Inc. on June 28, 2001, pursuant to a deed and land disposition agreement (LDA). The deed and LDA require compliance with the original Milbank Frawley Circle-East Urban Renewal Plan (Original Plan), approved by the City Planning Commission on August 19, 1992 (C920139HUM) and the New York City Council on October 8, 1992 (Reso. No. 920), which prohibits residential development within 100 feet of Park Avenue and restricts the sites to parking. On November 30, 2017, the Plan was amended (Second Amendment) by the New York City Council (Reso. No. 1743) to permit residential use within 100 feet of Park Avenue.

The sponsor intends to develop a proposed project consisting of one mixed-use building with 213 total units, of which at least 64 units will be affordable and will include retail and 21 parking spaces (the Project)

 

To facilitate the Project, HPD intends to modify the deed and LDA. The site is located in the Milbank Frawley Circle East Urban Renewal Area and is identified as a portion of Site 9 within the Plan. The deed and LDA associated with the parcel require compliance with the Original Plan, which specifically prohibits development within 100 feet of Park Avenue. HPD intends to amend the deed and LDA to remove the restrictions limiting the use of the parcel to parking, require compliance with the Second Amendment, which will be in effect until December 14, 2057, and to require at least 64 units in the project to be restricted as affordable housing.

rows.short_title: Bergen Green
rows.additional_description_1:
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on November 23, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed disposition of the real property identified below. The public hearing will be held via conference call.  Call  In: 1-646-992-2010 Access code: 2330 155 3512

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') has proposed the sale of the following City-owned property (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Brooklyn:

Address                                                                          Block/Lot

516 Bergen Street                                                         Block 1143 Lot 25                                                                                                        

Under HPD's Extremely Low and Low Income Affordability Program, sponsors purchase City-owned or privately owned land or vacant buildings and construct multifamily buildings in order to create affordable rental housing.  Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources including HPD, the New York City Housing Development Corporation, the State of New York, and the federal government.  Additional funding may also be provided from the syndication of low-income housing tax credits.  The newly constructed buildings provide rental housing to low-income families with a range of incomes from 30% to 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI).  Projects may include tiers of units with rents affordable to households earning up to 100% of AMI.  Subject to project underwriting, up to 30% of the units may be rented to formerly homeless families and individuals.

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to 516 Bergen Green Housing Development Fund Company, Inc. ('Sponsor') for the nominal price of one dollar per tax lot.  The Sponsor will also deliver an enforcement note and mortgage for the remainder of the appraised value (Land Debt).  The Sponsor will then construct one building containing approximately 111 rental dwelling units, plus one unit for a superintendent and community facility space on the Disposition Area. The Sponsor will provide approximately 23 replacement parking spaces for HPD.

The Land Debt or the Citys capital subsidy may be repayable out of resale or refinancing profits for a period of at least thirty (30) years following completion of construction.  The remaining balance, if any, may be forgiven at the end of the term.

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three (3) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.
